name: Sebastopol
description: Sebastopol is a cross domino game for four players (or three in variants) using a double-six set. Players build four arms from the double-six spinner; the first to play all tiles scores the pips in opponents' hands. Game is played to 60 points.

rules.objective: Be the first to play all your tiles (domino), or have the lowest pip total if the game blocks. First player to reach 60 points wins.
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal: Each player receives seven tiles.
2. Opening: The player with the double-six sets it in the center. Players in turn (clockwise) must play a tile in the sixes suit onto the double-six until four arms are started.
3. Play: Once all four arms are started, each player may add a tile to the end of any arm. Doubles are played across the line and do not branch. Unable to play: pass (turn passes).
4. Scoring: If a player dominoes, they score the total pips in opponents' hands. If the game blocks, the player with the lowest pip total wins and scores (sum of others' pips minus own). Game is played to 60 points.
keyRules: Player with the double-six starts; four arms of the spinner must be started before free play on any arm
Score is pips in opponents' hands when you domino; blocked game: lowest hand wins and scores
First to 60 points wins the game

strategy.basic: Play legally; try to domino before the hand blocks.
strategy.intermediate: There are seven tiles in the sixes suit; five are in the center when the spinner is complete. Watch which arms opponents avoid to infer missing suits.
strategy.advanced: Use the fact that when one of the two remaining sixes is played on an arm, that arm is blocked to all but the other six. Use opponent arm choices to read their hands.
tips: Observe which arms opponents do not play on to deduce which suits they lack.
Opening spinner exposes most suits on the arms; use this for inference.

variations.name: Ural (Russia) variant
variations.description: First deal started by double-six, then 5-5, 4-4 down to 0-0, then cycle. Players may extend arms without completing all four sides of the starting double. A double played face down blocks that arm; if all four arms blocked, game ends and scores as blocked. Double-six alone in hand at end counts 66 pips, 0-0 alone 100; with other tiles they count 12 and 0. First to 101 cumulative points wins. Three-handed: 7 tiles each, draw from boneyard if unable to play.

variations.name: Three-handed (Berndt)
variations.description: Nine tiles per player, one left in boneyard. Holder of the double-six sets it and draws the boneyard tile so hand stays at nine; play continues clockwise. If no one has the double-six it is in boneyard: turn it to start, same player who began last hand starts again.
